headline: Steady progress; we trim estimates and maintain 2.0x.

highlights: PAT stood at INR 3,123 Mn, below our estimate of INR 4,184 Mn, up 28.38% QoQ and 1.25% YoY.
Growth restarts on a secured, mortgage-led base: Disbursals rose 62% QoQ to INR 62.78 Bn, about 94% of them secured, with collection efficiency at 99.6%.

Funding costs are easing, but profit still leans on the legacy pool: Cost of funds fell to 9.8% (coupon basis) from 10.0% in Q1FY27, against a target of 9.3%; management expects a 25bps lending rate increase from November to widen spreads.
DA income was only INR 72 Mn as higher bank rates squeezed sell-down spreads; management expects a recovery over two to three quarters.
valuation: Funding costs are easing, but profit still leans on the legacy pool: Cost of funds fell to 9.8% (coupon basis) from 10.0% in Q1FY27, against a target of 9.3%; management expects a 25bps lending rate increase from November to widen spreads.
Valuation & View: H1FY27 PAT of INR 5,556 Mn was 37% of our earlier FY27E of INR 14,986 Mn, with recoveries and DA income running behind plan.

We maintain our BUY rating with a revised target price of INR 355 (from INR 360), based on 2.0x FY29E ABV of INR 177.0, implying 177.3% upside from the CMP of INR 128; the target is a 24 to 30 month plan-delivery value (12-month discounted INR 293).
watch: Execution risk remains high: profit still leans on the legacy pool and core PPOP excluding FV gains is negative.

Asset Quality & Governance • GNPA improved to 0.15% from 0.21% and NNPA to 0.11% from 0.15%; total provisions stand at 10.2% of the loan book. • BDO is co-sourcing internal audit; the CRO now reports to the Risk Management Committee and the CCO and Head of Internal Audit to the Audit Committee; a new chairperson is to be announced shortly.
